scope: Proposition 9.4 (A simultaneous good realization) of the manuscript “Smooth counterexamples to Yau's nodal upper bound in dimensions three and four” (preprints/Smooth-counterexamples-to-Yaus-nodal-upper-bound-in-dimensions-three-and-four-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 350 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8e4c129bdb0f2f45), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 48. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every predetermined pair of finite orders ℓ, J ≥ 0, all sufficiently large integers k admit a choice of the real Gaussian coefficients for which the smooth real function u satisfies u = u0 k outside a compact subset of U2, supp R ⋐ U2, R = (∆h + Λk)u, (9.9) sup P W−1 X |α|≤ℓ |∂α R| ≤ Cℓ,J k−J , (9.10) W−1 |∂α u| ≤ Cαk|α|+5 on P for every fixed multi-index α, |(u, k−1 du)| ≥ k−200 W on U2, (9.11) S(u) ≥ csk Z D B(x) dx. (9.12) Here cs > 0 is independent of the envelope and the accuracy orders. The constants Cℓ,J , Cα and the frequency threshold may depend on these fixed data, but the polynomial exponents in these bounds do not increase with the residual accuracy.
